newsitem.title: INDIA: India political crisis not seen hurting dlr inflow.
newsitem.headline: India political crisis not seen hurting dlr inflow.

text.p: Dollar inflows into India are unlikely to to be affected by the country's political uncertainty after a key partner on Sunday withdrew support to the ruling coalition government, a top official of the Bank of America said on Monday.
"There should not be any impact on dollar inflows," Arun Dobe, vice president and director (foreign exchange) at Bank of America in Bombay told Reuters.

"Those who are panicking and those who get panicked will both get burnt," Dobe said. The rupee opened mildly down at 35.9150/9350 on Monday compared to the previous close of 35.89/90 largely on political worries, dealers said.
It weakened to 35.95 in early deals on Monday, before recovering to 35.927/937 in latest trade.
Dobe said India's economic reforms are irreversible.
The Congress Party said it was withdrawing support to the ruling United Front governemnt on Sunday.
"If Congress comes to power, they can't get rid of what Chidambaram has done," Dobe said, referring to Indian finance minister's 1997/98 (April-March) budget.
"I don't see the rupee breaking 36.0 (per dollar)," Dobe said. "But even if it does, I would consider it an opportunity to sell dollars," he said.
